work.title: BRAND VOICE
work.subtitle: A voice scale and rewrite field guide
work.scope: A fictional voice guide for Plain Thread. Preferred phrases are editorial choices, not legal clearance, evidence of product capabilities or tested persuasion results.

pages.title: Give the voice a practical intention.
pages.lead: Plain Thread speaks with clarity, care and room for questions. The voice should help a reader understand a task without making the brand sound more certain than its evidence.
pages.body: This guide is an editorial direction for a fictional organisation. It does not establish product features, legal approval or tested communication performance. Use it to make choices visible rather than turn style into a claim.
pages.detail: We explain what we mean, say what remains uncertain and invite a relevant next step. That is a writing principle, not a guaranteed customer experience.
pages.question: Does this sentence make the task clearer without overstating certainty?

records.label: Clarity
records.prompt: Use concrete verbs and explain unfamiliar terms.

records.label: Care
records.prompt: Respect the reader’s context and ability to choose.

records.label: Honesty
records.prompt: State meaningful limits near the relevant claim.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Change tone when the situation changes.
pages.lead: A welcome can feel open. An instruction should be direct. A correction should be accountable. The underlying voice remains recognisable while the tone responds to the reader’s situation.
pages.body: Do not assume that every audience wants informality, humour or reassurance. A difficult issue may require a plain acknowledgement and a practical action rather than an upbeat brand flourish.
pages.detail: Review the reader’s task, risk and likely information need. Avoid using a style rule to conceal an unresolved service or product problem.
pages.question: What does the reader need from this message right now?

records.label: Welcome
records.prompt: Offer orientation without assuming enthusiasm.

records.label: Instruction
records.prompt: Name the action and its relevant condition.

records.label: Correction
records.prompt: Acknowledge the issue and state a verified next step.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Make the principles observable.
pages.lead: Prefer a specific action to a vague benefit. Keep a qualification beside its claim. Use a question when the next step genuinely depends on information the reader has.
pages.body: These principles help an editor explain a revision. They do not make every short sentence good or every technical term wrong. Keep the detail that the task requires.
pages.detail: Ask what the sentence lets a reader do or understand. If it only makes the brand sound impressive, look for the missing practical meaning.
pages.question: Which editing principle explains the change you propose?

records.label: Specific
records.prompt: Say what the reader can inspect or do.

records.label: Qualified
records.prompt: Retain conditions that affect the meaning.

records.label: Open
records.prompt: Leave room for a question when facts are incomplete.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Use a tone scale, not a personality score.
pages.lead: The working scale runs from reserved to expressive, formal to conversational and directive to exploratory. It is a discussion tool, not an audience measurement.
pages.body: For a concept explanation, use moderately conversational and exploratory language. For a procedural instruction, move toward directness while preserving care. The scale has no optimal numerical setting or conversion promise.
pages.detail: Explain the reason for each adjustment. A team should be able to disagree about a tone choice without pretending the scale has measured a person’s preference.
pages.question: Which dimension should change for this specific message?

records.label: Reserved to expressive
records.prompt: Use emphasis only when it serves understanding.

records.label: Formal to conversational
records.prompt: Match the setting without artificial familiarity.

records.label: Directive to exploratory
records.prompt: Be direct about actions, open about unknowns.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Choose words with a clear job.
pages.lead: Explore describes an invitation to inspect. Review describes a deliberate check. May preserves uncertainty when an outcome has not been established. None should be used mechanically.
pages.body: The phrase register offers eight authored alternatives to overstatement or vague instruction. A preferred phrase is not automatically appropriate; check whether it accurately describes the actual product and destination.
pages.detail: Avoid replacing every strong word with a weak one. The goal is accurate meaning, not blandness or a universal ban on confident language.
pages.question: What exactly does this word imply in the current sentence?

records.label: Explore
records.prompt: Use when the reader can inspect a real explanation.

records.label: Review
records.prompt: Use when a specific check is appropriate.

records.label: May
records.prompt: Use only when uncertainty genuinely matters to the claim.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Do not let familiar slogans hide claims.
pages.lead: Effortless, guaranteed and everyone can each imply more than a writer may intend. They can erase conditions, evidence requirements or differences between readers.
pages.body: The guide recommends checking or replacing these expressions in this fictional context. It does not declare them unlawful in every setting or provide legal clearance for a preferred alternative.
pages.detail: Record the implied claim before rewriting. A calmer adjective is not enough if the underlying statement still promises an unsupported outcome.
pages.question: Which implied claim needs evidence or a more accurate description?

records.label: Effortless
records.prompt: Can imply no meaningful work or conditions.

records.label: Guaranteed
records.prompt: Can imply a commitment that must actually exist.

records.label: Everyone can
records.prompt: Can hide access barriers or unsupported universality.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Show the change in meaning.
pages.lead: Before: Transform your workflow instantly. After: Review one step of your workflow and identify what needs context. The rewrite exchanges an unsupported promise for an inspectable activity.
pages.body: Before: Our solution works for everyone. After: Check whether this approach fits your task and access needs. A useful rewrite changes the claim, not only the mood of the sentence.
pages.subheading: Before and after, with a rationale
pages.detail: Neither example establishes a functioning service or verified capability. Use the comparison to discuss meaning before adapting it to actual copy.
pages.question: Does the revised sentence remove the unsupported implication?

records.label: Before
records.prompt: Transform your workflow instantly.

records.label: After
records.prompt: Review one step and identify what needs context.

records.label: Rationale
records.prompt: An activity replaces an unverified universal benefit.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Apply the voice in real message shapes.
pages.lead: Welcome: Start with the question you want to explore. Instruction: Add the source beside the passage before sharing it. Correction: The earlier note omitted a condition; please review the updated explanation.
pages.body: These are authored copy examples, not actual customer communications. A correction should describe the real issue and a verified next step; do not copy the example as though an event occurred.
pages.detail: A consistent voice can carry different tones. Keep essential instructions and uncertainty visible even when a short channel leaves little space.
pages.question: What would make this example accurate in the actual setting?

records.label: Welcome
records.prompt: Start with the question you want to explore.

records.label: Instruction
records.prompt: Add the source beside the passage before sharing.

records.label: Correction
records.prompt: Name the verified issue and the available next step.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Review meaning before polishing rhythm.
pages.lead: First check whether the statement is true and appropriately qualified. Then review whether the reader can understand the action. Only then refine tone, rhythm and repetition.
pages.body: An editorial checklist does not replace product, legal, accessibility or specialist review. Keep responsibility for those decisions explicit rather than assigning every concern to a voice editor.
pages.detail: Read the copy beside its destination or supporting artifact. A beautifully consistent phrase can still mislead if the underlying action cannot be fulfilled.
pages.question: Which unresolved meaning issue should stop stylistic approval?

records.label: Meaning check
records.prompt: Claims and conditions match appropriate evidence.

records.label: Task check
records.prompt: The reader can identify the next action.

records.label: Voice check
records.prompt: The tone supports the context without hiding limits.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.

pages.title: Keep a change record that explains why.
pages.lead: A living voice guide records the phrase, the reason for a revision and the context in which the change applies. A new preference should not silently rewrite past evidence.
pages.body: The supplied register is an authored version-one guide, not a history of approved organisational decisions. Test revisions against appropriate tasks and retain earlier wording when a review needs to understand the change.
pages.detail: Do not report a rewrite as proven to improve engagement unless a suitable evaluation supports that claim. Editorial preference and measured effect are different kinds of evidence.
pages.question: What reason would help another editor understand this revision?

records.label: Version
records.prompt: Authored guide v1; no organisational approval implied.

records.label: Reason
records.prompt: Replace vague or unsupported meaning with a specific task.

records.label: Outcome boundary
records.prompt: No measured persuasion or engagement effect supplied.

evidenceRows: 8 editorial rewrites; no tested winners or legal clearance.
